summary: The dissertation studies two gate-based quantum approaches to option pricing: variational circuit learning for European call payoffs and QFT-based pricing for European calls under Black-Scholes. The variational search reports best European-call fits around MSE 0.0396 (VAns-based) and 0.0431 (circuit-based), while the QFT pricing method shows much better pricing accuracy than the other compared approaches but still depends on efficient state preparation and, for the first discretization, a Hadamard test.
